neighbours.label: a noun or adjective naming the magnitude of a quantity (' level', ' levels', ' volume', ' high', ' low') in economic or physical description; the - pole is whether that quantity changes ('constant', 'grows', 'worse')
fire: Economists noted that the country's debt level is now the highest in Europe.
The patient had high levels of sugar in her blood at the first visit.
An ideal gas is made of particles that occupy zero volume.
Interest rates in the region remain at historically low levels this year.
The current high price of grain has hurt poor families most.
Noise levels near the airport exceed the legal limit at night.
The tank was filled to a volume of forty litres before the test.
Unemployment in the town stayed at a low level throughout the decade.
quiet: Economists noted that the country's debt is now discussed across Europe.
The patient had sugar in her tea at the first visit to the clinic.
An ideal gas is made of particles that never stick to one another.
Interest rates in the region are set by the central bank each month.
The current price of grain is printed in the morning newspaper.
Planes near the airport take off every few minutes at night.
The tank was filled with water from the river before the test.
Unemployment in the town was a topic of debate throughout the decade.

notes: Card: ' high' x3, ' levels' x3, ' level' x2, ' low' x2, ' volume', ' GDP'. - pole: ' constant', ' increased', ' same', ' worse', ' static'.
